answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that accrues slowly, like a glacier carving a valley: a new agent starts on the lowest terrace with tiny limits, and only earns higher limits after a long history of useful, verified work. Each transaction then carries a pulse of verifiable cost - a small proof of work or bonded stake - so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive while honest agents climb steadily. Sybils freeze at the bottom; real contributors rise.
